answer: A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. Because the forge sample is drawn from the tide beacon, the nebula audit reveals the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is recorded per key. A random 1% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. That is 17 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
